name: Grime
summary: 140 BPM that feels like 70: a halftime snare on beat 3, sparse angular kicks on awkward off-16ths, and negative space for the MC. Snares are dry gunshot cracks or rimshot clicks that may leave the backbeat entirely; hats are minimal or absent and off-kilter clicks, claves and congas fill in instead, all programmed straight on the grid.

sounds.kick: Dry, mid-heavy drum-machine or FL-stock kick with a hard click; short and often distorted, never a long 808 boom (the square-wave bass owns the sub).
sounds.snare: Dry 'gunshot' snare or heavily compressed clap, sometimes a literal gunshot FX layered under the snare; rimshot/side-stick clicks as the second voice.
sounds.hats: Sparse 8th-note closed hats or none; when present they are thin, bright and unswung, with sudden fast-hat bursts then silence.
sounds.percussion: Icy clicks, claves, woodblocks, congas and cowbells placed on awkward 16ths; ringtone/PlayStation-era lo-fi hits.
sounds.cymbals: Crash only for 8-bar markers and reloads; no ride.

machines: FruityLoops stock kit (140 default tempo) and PlayStation Music 2000 samples — the actual tools of the eski era
Roland TR-808 — snare, clap, cowbell and clave layers
Casio RZ-1 / SK-1 — 8-bit crunchy sampled hits for lo-fi texture
Boss DR-660 / DR-202 — dry 90s hip-hop kits close to the FL presets
Korg Triton / Trinity drum presets — the mid-2000s grime staple
Sound-effects libraries — gunshots, glass, metallic clicks
references: Ruff Sqwad — Functions on the Low (2004)
